\subsection{Simulation on Replayed Production Sessions}\label{sec:sim}

The simulator replays the production sessions of \S\ref{sec:exp-traces}
against a simulated replica, so the workload side is measured and only
the replica is modelled: iterations of length $\max(\omega+\beta K_B,\
n\,a)$ for a batch of $n$ decoding turns holding $K_B$ tokens of KV, so
decode is a bandwidth PS with the demand~\eqref{eq:decode} and prefill
is a FIFO server that receives the compute the batch leaves; resident KV
is a prefix, and a turn re-prefills what was evicted with the
work~\eqref{eq:prefill}. The one uncalibrated element is the cost
model: $a=2\cdot10^{-5}$, $b=4\cdot10^{-10}$ (attention overtakes the
dense term at $50$k tokens), $\omega=2\cdot10^{-4}$ and
$\beta=2\cdot10^{-9}$ seconds per token, so no number below is a
measurement of a serving system. Before the replay, every proposition
is checked as a named test with fixed seeds and an explicit tolerance
under its own assumptions and with one assumption dropped on synthetic
sessions (Appendix~\ref{app:sim}; of \simChecks{} checks,
\simChecksPassed{} pass): the closed forms are reproduced within their
confidence intervals or 2\,\%; forced misses at an M/G/1 server land at
the upper end of the bracket of Proposition~\ref{prop:price}, where the
exact PK difference lies, and on the two-resource replica they raise
the prefill queue and leave the decode batch unchanged; the saturating
$\varphi$ misjudges an exact batch cap by the sign of the work
$\mathrm{CV}^2$; on synthetic two-class sessions the priced eviction
orders beat shortest-first only within seed noise while LRU is worst
everywhere, and the admission cap decides whether the replica thrashes
(hit rate $0.99$ at a cap of 16, most seeds thrashing at 32); and over
four replicas with a shared link the load at which always moving beats
affinity rises as the link slows, following $\rho^*$ of~\eqref{eq:rhostar}
for a fast link and reached only once the link itself is $97\,\%$ busy
for a slow one. Confidence intervals are 95\,\% batch means or, where
stated, across independent seeds.

\input{sim/tab-trace}

\paragraph{Replayed production sessions.} Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace}
plays each real session's appends, outputs, think times and length on
the replica. A gap above ten minutes
starts a new session, whose first prompt is the whole accumulated
context (median \wkFirstCtxSplit k tokens against \wkFirstCtxNew k for
a genuinely new session; \wkSplitShare\,\% of replayed sessions start
this way); splitting at thirty minutes instead leaves $W_q$, the PK
wait and TTFT within seed noise while the live count doubles with the
longer sessions (Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-split}). Three things follow. First, with no eviction every
follow-up turn hits and the prefill work of follow-up turns still has
$\mathrm{CV}^2=\simTraceOpenCvMin$--$\simTraceOpenCvMax$, from the
appends alone; the mean TTFT of
\simTraceOpenTtftMin--\simTraceOpenTtftMax\,s is set by the cold first
prompts, which every turn behind them waits for. Second, once the pool
is finite the cap on live sessions binds throughout the run, the
replica is a closed system of $N$ sessions and the entry queue grows
for the whole horizon (up to \simTraceEntryMaxHours{} hours of mean
wait). At the tight cap the hit rate stays at or above
\simTraceTightHitMin{} and the hit/miss mixture supplies
\simTraceTightMixMin--\simTraceTightMixMax\,\% of the variance of
follow-up prefill work, the simulated version of the split of
Table~\ref{tab:cv2} once eviction is active; at the loose cap the
replica thrashes, the hit rate falls to at most \simTraceLooseHitMax{}
and the mean TTFT exceeds \simTraceLooseTtftMin\,s. Third, the PK wait
computed from the measured $\lambda$, $\E[S]$ and $\E[S^2]$ of the
prefill queue is above the observed wait in every cell, by a factor of
\simTracePkRatioMin{} to \simTracePkRatioMax; the largest factors are in
the cells with $\rho$ near one, where the open formula is near its pole,
but the direction holds at $\rho=0.25$ with five sessions live, as
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} says it must for exponential work. For
the price itself, Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-price} forces a share
$\delta$ of resident follow-up turns to miss in the open-pool
configuration and compares the rise of the number in the prefill stage
with the bracket of Proposition~\ref{prop:price} from the baseline's
measured moments and with the finite-source price of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite}. With \simPriceLiveMin{} to
\simPriceLiveMax{} sessions live in the baseline, the open bracket's
lower end overstates the observed rise by \simPriceOverMin{} to
\simPriceOverMax{} times, and at $\delta\ge3\,\%$ the added work puts
the open queue past its pole while the capped replica stays finite; the
Markovian finite-source price, which ignores the second moment of the
work, understates the rise by \simPriceFiniteRatioMin{} to
\simPriceFiniteRatioMax{} times; and the cap $N-L_P$ holds in
\simPriceCapHolds{} cell. The rise a real workload shows lies between
the two prices, which is what a finite-source price with the work's
second moment would have to capture, and E2 has to report the number of
live sessions next to the load.
